+catalog — and gates both on being inside a tag via `tokenize`. Hover shows the

 ### Conventions worth knowing

@@ -286,13 +286,17 @@ parse buys nothing. Instead:
 * The server gates hover and completion on being *inside a tag*, decided by the
   engine's own `tokenize` (not a re-implemented lexer) — the offset must fall in a
   `tag` span and not in an interior `string`/`number` literal. *Hover* on a known
-  operation reports its kind, arity, alias/synonym relationship, and a signature
-  *synthesised from the kind* — never prose, which lives in the spec and would only
-  drift. *Completion* inside a tag offers the operations, excluding deprecated
-  aliases (they still hover, so existing code is explained) and sorting scoped
-  variables after helpers.
-
-There is intentionally **no per-operation documentation string**: the schema
-carries none, and duplicating the spec's prose into code would create a second
-source to drift. Hover/completion surface only what the engine actually knows.
-Covered by `test:lsp` (unit + protocol) and the real-IDE test path.
+  operation reports its kind, arity, alias/synonym relationship, a signature
+  *synthesised from the kind*, and its one-line prose doc. *Completion* inside a tag
+  offers the operations, excluding deprecated aliases (they still hover, so existing
+  code is explained) and sorting scoped variables after helpers.
+
+The prose comes from a **required `doc` field on `OperationDef`** (a follow-up to
+this amendment): the single source, populated for every operation and
+compiler-enforced by the `valDef`/`gen` smart constructors, so an operation cannot
+ship undocumented and there is no parallel doc table to drift. (This supersedes
+this amendment's first cut, which deliberately carried *no* doc string for exactly
+the drift fear — solved instead by making the prelude itself the one source.)
+Scoped variables live outside `operationDefs` and carry no doc, so hover simply
+omits the line. The long-form reference prose stays in `prelude.adoc`; `doc` is the
+one-line summary. Covered by `test:lsp` (unit + protocol) and the real-IDE path.

@@ -7,7 +7,7 @@ approximating it. See `docs/modules/ROOT/pages/adr-0017-editor-support-lsp.adoc`
 | --- | --- |
 | `token-vocabulary.json` | **The single source of truth.** Each engine token `kind` → its `role` (`tag`/`interior`), LSP semantic-token `type`/`modifiers`, and TextMate `tmScopes`. The three consumers below all derive from it. |
 | `flatbars.tmLanguage.json` | The TextMate **fallback** grammar — the *floor*. The well-known Handlebars grammar, re-identified as `source.flatbars` and extended for all four dialects (inverse, Mustache inheritance, set delimiters, MaxBars operators), keeping its standard scope names so themes colour FlatBars familiarly. Colours **only template syntax + a leading YAML front-matter block** — host text is left plain (a FlatBars template's output need not be HTML). Best-effort and non-authoritative: stateless, FullBars-flavoured, and it cannot follow a set-delimiter *switch* — the LSP corrects those. |
-| `lsp/` | **`flatbars-lsp`** — the authoritative server (the *ceiling*). Embeds the committed `flatbars-js` bundle and answers `semanticTokens/full` from `tokenize`, `publishDiagnostics` from the recovering parser (ADR-023), and `hover`/`completion` from `editors/operations.json` (the prelude schema projected by `FullBars.Catalog.operations`). Stateful by construction, so set delimiters and dialects are correct. |
+| `lsp/` | **`flatbars-lsp`** — the authoritative server (the *ceiling*). Embeds the committed `flatbars-js` bundle and answers `semanticTokens/full` from `tokenize`, `publishDiagnostics` from the recovering parser (ADR-023), and `hover`/`completion` from `editors/operations.json` (the prelude schema projected by `FullBars.Catalog.operations`, incl. each operation's one-line `OperationDef.doc`). Stateful by construction, so set delimiters and dialects are correct. |
 | `vscode/` | The VS Code extension: contributes the fallback grammar and spawns `flatbars-lsp`. `dist/` is a git-ignored build product (`npm run build`). |
 | `jetbrains/` | The JetBrains plugin (Gradle/Kotlin): bundles the fallback grammar via a `TextMateBundleProvider` (all IDEs) and, on Ultimate (`-PwithLsp`), spawns `flatbars-lsp` through the platform LSP API. `build/` and the synced resources are git-ignored. |
